lines: מָה אַדִּיר אַתָּה, מָה אַדִּיר אַתָּה
מָה אַדִּיר אַתָּה, מָה אַדִּיר אַתָּה

review: The hymn is the created order answering the Creator: 2:1–4 is Ps 8:4 (כִּי אֶרְאֶה שָׁמֶיךָ מַעֲשֵׂה אֶצְבְּעֹתֶיךָ) with Ps 19:2, 3:3–4 Ps 104:10 (הַמְשַׁלֵּחַ מַעְיָנִים בַּנְּחָלִים) with Ps 104:12 (עֲלֵי־עֳפָאָיו תִּשְׁכּוֹן), and 4:2–4 Isa 53:10–11 with 1 Pet 2:24–25.

1:1–4 repeats the couplet, as the print does: the Arabic gives نَفْسِي تُغَنِّي يَا مُخَلِّصِي / مَا أَعْظَمَك twice and then again, so the Hebrew keeps all four lines rather than compressing the stanza to one couplet. מָה אַדִּיר אַתָּה is the psalm's exclamation (Ps 8:2, מָה־אַדִּיר שִׁמְךָ) and not the modern 'how great'.

2:2 בְּגַלְגַּלֵּי מְרוֹמִים — the Arabic فِي الْأَفْلَاك is the astronomical 'spheres'; biblical Hebrew has גַּלְגַּל only in the vision of Ezek 10:13, and the plural with מְרוֹמִים keeps the sense of the revolving heavens without importing the later cosmology as a doctrine.

3:4 וַהֲמוֹנוֹ יָבֹא עִם־נְעִימוֹת — the Arabic خَرِيرُهُ يَأْتِي مَعَ الْأَلْحَان is 'its murmur comes with melodies'; הָמוֹן is the biblical sound of many waters (Ezek 43:2, קוֹל מַיִם רַבִּים) and נְעִימוֹת the psalm's word for sweet music (Ps 81:3), so the stream is both noise and song.

4:1 הִתְעַנָּה — the Arabic does not say 'suffered' here, only that the Lord gave Himself; the Hebrew adds the self-humbling of Isa 53:7 and Phil 2:8, because the stanza's argument is that the Creator of stanza 2 is the Servant of stanza 4.
